results.reason: Identifies Schedule §1.1 (ship date from Verdane's plant) vs MSA §1.3 (Rochester delivery). Explains that late delivery, risk and the invoicing/payment trigger key off the ship date, and that Harlow loses transit-delay remedies.
Recommends conforming the Schedule definition to the MSA (delivery at Rochester) and adding an order-of-precedence clause under which the MSA controls.

Identifies §4.3 as covering all housings and similar components worldwide, against the Term Sheet's Series 7/US bargain. Explains that it blocks other sourcing and non-US plants, and recommends narrowing to Series 7 Housings in the US.

Identifies §15.2 as one-sided (Verdane may assign without consent; Harlow needs consent) and notes the competitor and Specifications risk. Recommends prior written consent, a bar on assignment to competitors, and a change-of-control termination right.

Identifies that Amendment §2 removes gross negligence and the IP indemnity from the carve-outs, bringing those losses under the 12-month fee cap. Recommends rejecting §2 and restoring the original exclusions.
States the cap is fees paid in the prior 12 months and lists the original exclusions: gross negligence, willful misconduct and the IP indemnity.
States the Term Sheet §3 exclusivity covers Series 7 Housings in the US and uses it as the baseline for comparing §4.3.
Notes New York law under MSA §16.1, includes an assumptions section, and expressly cites no cases or statutes, flagging the law as needing verification.
Structured partner memo. Each issue gives location, why it matters and a recommended fix; issues are ranked by importance; there is an assumptions and open-facts section.
Expressly treats the Term Sheet as evidence of the deal, not a problem document. Lists term and payment as checked and not defects.
Section citations are consistent with the documents, party benefits are correctly attributed, and no legal authority is fabricated.
